date.label: Undated Judges narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Judges 5 explicitly mentions Taanach and the waters of Megiddo, unlike Judges 4’s battlefield emphasis, and the song specifies Taanach, Megiddo, and the Kishon while Judges 4 highlights Tabor and the Kishon approach
claims.evidence: Judges 5:19 and Judges 4:12–16 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated. JADD-001 merged (same ground): the song's Taanach/Megiddo/Kishon specification versus Judges 4's Tabor and Kishon approach is one contrast, not a second independent claim.

claims.claim: Judges 5 is a victory song attributed to Deborah and Barak. Its date of composition is debated; do not assign a definite pre-monarchic year or label it indisputably the oldest Hebrew poem.
claims.evidence: Judges 5 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Qualified textual claim only; no external historical certification. Grounded by Mayfield's survey (verified, full text read, pp. 306–335), which concludes scholars differ concerning the compositional date of the song, and by Frolov's late-date position via his Bible Odyssey summary (verified, read in full).

claims.claim: The text depicts Deborah exercising judicial and prophetic authority
claims.evidence: Judges 4:4–5 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

connections.note: Victory hymn and divine-warrior poetic traditions (Exodus 15:1–21). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.

Poem connects Shamgar to the insecure travel setting (Judges 5:6–7). What they share is a literary relationship between texts; agreement among biblical passages is not equivalent to independent confirmation of the episodes.
Theophany from the south shares poetic imagery (Psalm 68:7–8). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.
